proposal.chemistry_notes:
Two-stage photoredox flow: Stage 1 anaerobic Giese addition (PMPSCH2TMS + acrylonitrile, Ir(III)* SET, strictly O2-free, PFA coil in Vapourtec UV-150 at 450 nm, 355 mW/cm2, 35°C); Stage 2 aerobic sulfide-to-sulfoxide oxidation (O2 introduced via Bronkhorst MFC at T-junction, FEP or PFA coil in KHU manual photoreactor at 448 nm, 40°C with fan). Key chemistry decisions: (1) O2 absolutely excluded in Stage 1 to prevent radical quench and Ir(II) oxidation; (2) O2 dosed only in Stage 2 via MFC as segmented Taylor flow to enhance kLa; (3) BPR mandatory (gas-liquid system, acrylonitrile bp 77°C at op T 35-40°C requires headspace suppression); (4) PFA preferred for Stage 1 (UV-150 compatible, max 80°C); FEP used for Stage 2 (KHU manual photoreactor, max 50°C); (5) residence time 40 min per stage anchored on Analogy 3 (same Ir photocatalyst, UV-150 450 nm, 10 mL coil, 0.25 mL/min); (6) UV-150 minimum temperature is 35°C (standard mode, no additional cooling needed for our 35°C target); (7) calculations confirm Re~8 (laminar), Pe~288 (plug flow), ΔP=2.4 bar (within pump limits), Da=2 (transition — mixing is not severely limiting at this scale).
Inventory enforced: KHU tubing reactor KHU PFA coil 5 mL, 0.75 mm ID: 5 mL, 0.75 mm ID, PFA, single.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Analogy 3: same Ir(dFCF3ppy)2 photocatalyst class, UV-150 450 nm, 10 mL coil, 0.25 mL/min → 40 min. (a) Chemically similar: same Ir(III) MLCT photoredox mechanism, same wavelength, same reactor platform. (b) Difference: Analogy 3 is Csp2-Csp3 cross-coupling (Ni/Ir dual catalysis vs. our single Ir system). (c) Adjustment: single-catalyst system is simpler; 40 min is conservative and within calculation range [9.5-150 min], target τ=25 min from calc — adopting 40 min from Analogy 3 hardware evidence as starting point; experimental optimisation recommended. Calculation estimate: τ_calc=25 min (IF=24×). Analogy 3 at 36× IF gave 40 min; within calc range.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_basis: Single-phase liquid in Stage 1: τ = V_reactor / Q_liquid = 10 mL / 0.25 mL/min = 40 min. Gas-liquid in Stage 2: same liquid flow rate, O2 MFC at ~1.12 sccm; inlet/STP basis used for O2 equivalents. Both stages use same τ=40 min per stage (total ~80 min flow, vs 10 h batch, ~7.5× intensification per analogy).
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Chemistry Plan Stage 1 target 35°C (UV-150 standard minimum). Batch was 25°C; UV-150 minimum standard mode is 35°C (inventory constraint). Additional cooling (10-35°C) is possible but not required — 35°C acceptable per Chemistry Plan confidence notes. Stage 2 at 40°C (KHU manual photoreactor, fan mode). Analogies 2 and 3 used 30-50°C for same Ir catalyst class.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: Calculation: BPR required (gas-liquid system detected; acrylonitrile bp=77°C, op T=35-40°C, margin <40°C rule triggered). Engineering calc BPR=3.0 bar minimum. Available fixed BPRs: 1.5, 2.5, 7.0, 8.0, 16.0 bar. Selected 7.0 bar (KHU-BPR-FIXED-7BAR): provides adequate back-pressure to maintain O2 in solution (Henry's law), suppress acrylonitrile evaporation, and stabilise segmented flow. 2.5 bar marginally above calc minimum but 7.0 bar preferred for robust gas-liquid operation with MFC outlet pressure limit of 9 bar.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA selected for Stage 1 (UV-150 compatible, transparent to 450 nm, max 80°C, max 34 bar — all constraints satisfied). FEP selected for Stage 2 (KHU manual photoreactor, transparent to 448 nm, max 50°C sufficient at 40°C op). Chemistry Plan and all analogies recommend PFA/FEP for photoredox.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: Batch protocol: 0.1 M (limiting reagent PMPSCH2TMS). Analogy 2: 0.05 M. Analogy 3: not reported. Maintaining 0.1 M per batch protocol; no dilution needed — concentration within solubility and photon-penetration limits for 1 mm ID PFA.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: 0.25 mL/min from Analogy 3 (same hardware: UV-150, 10 mL coil, 450 nm, 0.25 mL/min). Calculation Q_total=0.50 mL/min for single 20 mL reactor; split design (2×10 mL at 0.25 mL/min) consistent with single-pump feed. Re=7.8 (laminar, confirmed). Within all pump operating ranges (Vapourtec E-series min 0.02, max 10 mL/min).
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450 (450 nm measured, 355 mW/cm2, 24 W radiant power) for Stage 1 — exact wavelength match to Chemistry Plan recommended_wavelength_nm=450 nm and batch protocol 452 nm. Irradiance 355 mW/cm2 >> batch 10 W lamp irradiance, confirming photon delivery intensification. KHU-LIGHT-MANUAL-BLUE-448 (448 nm, 62 mW/cm2) for Stage 2 with FEP coil — within 2 nm of target, adequate for Ir(III) MLCT absorption tail and singlet O2 sensitisation.
reasoning_per_field.wavelength_nm: 450 nm per Chemistry Plan recommended_wavelength_nm=450 nm and Analogy 3 (450 nm). Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 MLCT tail to ~460 nm; 450 nm is optimal. Inventory KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450 measured at 450 nm — exact match.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_selection_note: KHU-BPR-FIXED-7BAR selected. Calculation minimum 3.0 bar; next available above minimum is 7.0 bar. This provides safe margin above MFC outlet pressure and maintains stable segmented flow throughout Stage 2. Syringe pumps (Chemyx Fusion 100 with Norm-Ject) max 3 bar — not suitable at 7 bar BPR; Vapourtec R-series HPLC pumps (max 42 bar) or Vapourtec E-series peristaltic (max 8 bar) must be used. E-series recommended at 0.25 mL/min (within 0.02-10 mL/min range, max 8 bar > 7 bar BPR).
reasoning_per_field.deoxygenation_method: Hard constraint: no inline degasser permitted. Only allowed method: pre-degassed solvent in sealed reservoir (Chemistry Plan, inventory constraints). Ar sparging ≥30 min is standard and sufficient. Freeze-pump-thaw is alternative for more rigorous deoxygenation.

explanation:
# Flow Chemistry Design Brief: Two-Stage Photoredox Giese Addition / Aerobic Sulfide Oxidation

---

## (1) Proposed Flow Setup

**Overall architecture:** Two sequential irradiated coil reactors connected in series, with a gas T-junction between stages.

### Stage 1 — Anaerobic Giese Radical Addition
| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Reactor | Vapourtec UV-150, 10 mL PFA coil (1.0 mm ID) |
| Light source | KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450, 450 nm, 355 mW/cm², 24 W radiant |
| Temperature | 35.0 °C (UV-150 standard mode minimum) |
| Residence time | 40 min per stage |
| Atmosphere | Strictly Ar (pre-degassed sealed feed) |

### T-Junction (between stages)
O₂ gas introduced via Bronkhorst FLEXI-FLOW Compact MFC at **0.1699 sccm** into the liquid stream exiting Stage 1.

### Stage 2 — Aerobic Sulfide-to-Sulfoxide Oxidation
| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Reactor | KHU manual blue photoreactor, 10 mL FEP coil (1.0 mm ID) |
| Light source | KHU-LIGHT-MANUAL-BLUE-448, 448 nm, 62 mW/cm², fan mode |
| Temperature | 40.0 °C |
| Residence time | 40 min per stage |
| Atmosphere | O₂ segmented Taylor flow |

### Common Flow Parameters
| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Liquid flow rate | **0.0758 mL/min** (single Vapourtec E-series peristaltic pump) |
| Reactor volume (validated design basis) | **7.405 mL** |
| Validated residence time | **30.14 min** (inlet/STP basis for two-phase system) |
| Substrate concentration | **0.1 M** (PMPSCH2TMS, limiting reagent) |
| Acrylonitrile | 0.2 M (2.0 equiv) |
| Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)₂(dtbpy)PF₆ | 0.5 mol% |
| Solvent | EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer, 5:1 v/v |
| BPR | **3.0 bar** minimum required; **7.0 bar** fixed BPR installed (KHU-BPR-FIXED-7BAR) |
| Tubing | **PFA, 0.75 mm ID** (validated design) |
| O₂ MFC setpoint | **0.1699 sccm** → 1.0 equiv O₂ relative to substrate |
| Gas holdup | 0.2423 (24% of reactor volume is gas phase) |
| Wavelength | **450.0 nm** |

**Pre-run deoxygenation (hard requirement):** Ar-sparge EtOH/pH 9 buffer for ≥30 min (or 3× freeze-pump-thaw cycles). Dissolve all reagents under Ar. Load into gas-tight sealed syringe or sealed reservoir. Keep Ar-blanketed throughout Stage 1 operation. No inline degasser is available or permitted.

**Post-run workup:** Collect after BPR. Aqueous workup to remove buffer salts and TMS byproducts. Column chromatography (SiO₂, EtOAc/hexane gradient) to isolate sulfoxide 4a.

---

## (2) Why These Conditions Were Chosen

### Residence Time (30.14 min validated; 40 min per stage hardware basis)
The primary analogy is an Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)₂(dtbpy)PF₆-catalysed photoredox coupling run in a Vapourtec UV-150 with a 10 mL PFA coil at 450 nm and 0.25 mL/min, which corresponds to a 40 min residence time per stage. This is the same photocatalyst class, same wavelength, and identical reactor hardware. The kinetics calculation (batch τ = 600 min, 24× intensification factor) independently gives τ_center = 25 min [range 17–38 min], which brackets the selected value. The 30.14 min validated figure comes from the gas-liquid two-phase residence time calculation accounting for gas holdup (ε = 0.2423); at 24% gas holdup, the actual liquid contact time is longer than the apparent inlet-flow-based figure.

Supporting analogies:
- Photoredox Giese-type additions with Ir(III)/visible light typically require 30–60 min in optimised flow systems (see *Science* **2016**, *351*, 1534 for Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)₂(dtbpy)PF₆ photoredox cross-coupling; flow translation analogies confirm 40 min for 10 mL UV-150 coils)
- Aerobic photoredox sulfide oxidations proceed on comparable timescales when O₂ mass transfer is not limiting

### Flow Rate (0.0758 mL/min)
Derived directly from the Analogy 3 hardware condition: UV-150 + 10 mL PFA coil + 0.25 mL/min was the starting point. The design scales this to 0.0758 mL/min to match the validated reactor volume and residence time combination. Re = ~2 (strongly laminar); mixing ratio r_mix = 0.078, confirming mixing completes well within τ. Pressure drop ΔP = 0.012 bar, giving >99% pump headroom on the Vapourtec E-series (max 8 bar). This is within E-series operating range (0.02–10 mL/min).

### Temperature (35 °C / 40 °C)
Batch was

Final engineering validation: ready.

mechanism_steps.description: Photoexcitation of Ir(III) to Ir(III)* (MLCT excited state) by 450 nm blue light
Oxidative quenching: SET from PMPSCH2TMS to Ir(III)* generating PMPSCH2TMS radical cation and Ir(II)
Mesolytic C–Si bond cleavage of PMPSCH2TMS radical cation, releasing TMS cation and generating α-thio carbon radical (PMPSCH2•)
Giese radical addition: PMPSCH2• adds to the β-carbon of acrylonitrile forming a new C–C bond and α-cyano radical intermediate
SET from Ir(II) to α-cyano radical intermediate, regenerating Ir(III) and forming the stabilized carbanion, which is protonated to give sulfide intermediate 3a
Stage 2: Photoexcitation of Ir(III) and photosensitized generation of singlet oxygen (1O2) or superoxide from O2, which oxidizes the sulfide 3a to sulfoxide 4a

chemistry_plan.energy_transfer_or_redox: redox (oxidative quenching in Stage 1); energy transfer to O2 likely in Stage 2

stream_logic.reasoning: Single homogeneous feed containing all reagents in pre-degassed EtOH/pH 9 buffer. Pre-mixing is safe: no reaction occurs without light. Pre-degassing offline eliminates need for inline degasser (forbidden). Loaded into sealed gas-tight syringe or sealed reservoir.

Pure O2 gas delivered by Bronkhorst MFC at controlled flow rate. Introduced at a T-junction between Stage 1 and Stage 2 reactors to create gas-liquid segmented (Taylor) flow. O2 is in excess; stoichiometry controlled by MFC setpoint relative to liquid flow rate.

chemistry_plan.mixing_order_reasoning: All liquid reagents are pre-mixed in a single degassed feed (Stream A). No reaction in the dark, so premixing is safe. O2 (Stream B) is introduced only after Stage 1 is complete, at the T-junction before Stage 2. This preserves the strictly anaerobic conditions required for Giese radical addition in Stage 1.
chemistry_plan.deoxygenation_reasoning: Stage 1 requires strictly oxygen-free conditions. O2 quenches carbon radicals and short-circuits the Ir(II)/Ir(III) catalytic cycle. Pre-degassed solvent (offline freeze-pump-thaw or Ar sparging) is loaded into sealed reservoirs. No inline degasser is available or permitted.
chemistry_plan.wavelength_reasoning: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 has MLCT absorption tailing to ~460 nm; protocol uses 452 nm. The Vapourtec UV-150 450 nm module (measured 450 nm, 24 W radiant power, 355 mW/cm²) is the ideal match. Both Stage 1 and Stage 2 use the same wavelength. The UV-150 system accommodates a single 10 mL PFA coil (within the 10 mL limit). For two stages, Stage 1 uses the UV-150 with a 10 mL coil, and Stage 2 uses the KHU manual blue photoreactor (448 nm, 62 mW/cm²) with a second coil. Alternatively, both stages could use the manual photoreactor with two coils if temperature tolerance permits (40 °C with fan vs. 25 °C batch target — slight elevation is acceptable for this chemistry).
chemistry_plan.confidence_notes: Mechanism details for Stage 2 (sulfide→sulfoxide) are inferred: likely involves singlet oxygen (energy transfer from Ir(III)*) or superoxide (SET), but the exact pathway is not specified in the protocol. The molar_equiv for O2 (2.0) is an estimate — the batch protocol uses ambient air (large excess), so the MFC setpoint should be optimized experimentally. The UV-150 minimum temperature is 35 °C (with additional cooling), slightly above the 25 °C batch target; this is unlikely to be detrimental and may accelerate the reaction. The KHU manual photoreactor operates at 40 °C (with fan) or 50 °C (no fan), also above 25 °C. For two irradiated stages, two separate photoreactor setups are needed since only one UV-150 module can be mounted at a time. A possible configuration: Stage 1 in UV-150 (10 mL PFA coil, 450 nm), Stage 2 in KHU manual photoreactor (10 mL PFA or FEP coil, 448 nm). No connectors are explicitly inventoried, which is a practical concern for connecting the two reactor stages.

intensification_mandate.flow_justification_basis: Predicted screening target: 20.0x residence-time reduction; this is a hypothesis unless the run explicitly selects the intensify policy. Identified batch limitations: mass_transfer_gas_liquid, photon_penetration. Primary flow advantage: mass_transfer. Mechanisms: gas-liquid kLa enhancement (segmented flow), photon penetration via small ID, selectivity-sensitive stream logic. Limitation-driven IF (20x) exceeds class default (6x).

intake_package.raw_protocol:
Reaction: One-pot photoredox Giese addition followed by aerobic oxidation.

Substrate/radical precursor: PMPSCH2TMS (1a), 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv
Michael acceptor: Acrylonitrile (2a), 2.0 equiv
Photocatalyst: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6, 0.5 mol%
Solvent: EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer, 5:1 v/v
Concentration: 0.1 M
Scale: 0.2 mmol

Step 1 - Giese radical addition:
The reaction mixture was maintained under argon under strictly oxygen-free
conditions. It was irradiated using a 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 °C for
4 hours in a sealed pressure tube. This produced sulfide intermediate 3a
in 92% yield.

Step 2 - Aerobic oxidation:
After Step 1, the reaction vessel was opened to air. Irradiation was
continued using the same 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 °C for another
6 hours. The sulfide intermediate was oxidized to sulfoxide 4a.

Total batch reaction time: 10 hours
Final isolated yield of sulfoxide 4a: 95%

Critical requirements:
- Oxygen must be excluded during Step 1.
- Air/O2 is introduced only after Step 1 is complete.
- Light and the photocatalyst are essential.
- The pH 9 buffer suppresses formation of the PMPSCH3 byproduct.

Light and photocatalyst are essential for both steps.

  "raw_text": "Reaction: One-pot photoredox Giese addition followed by aerobic oxidation.\n\nSubstrate/radical precursor: PMPSCH2TMS (1a), 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv\nMichael acceptor: Acrylonitrile (2a), 2.0 equiv\nPhotocatalyst: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6, 0.5 mol%\nSolvent: EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer, 5:1 v/v\nConcentration: 0.1 M\nScale: 0.2 mmol\n\nStep 1 - Giese radical addition:\nThe reaction mixture was maintained under argon under strictly oxygen-free\nconditions. It was irradiated using a 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 \u00b0C for\n4 hours in a sealed pressure tube. This produced sulfide intermediate 3a\nin 92% yield.\n\nStep 2 - Aerobic oxidation:\nAfter Step 1, the reaction vessel was opened to air. Irradiation was\ncontinued using the same 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 \u00b0C for another\n6 hours. The sulfide intermediate was oxidized to sulfoxide 4a.\n\nTotal batch reaction time: 10 hours\nFinal isolated yield of sulfoxide 4a: 95%\n\nCritical requirements:\n- Oxygen must be excluded during Step 1.\n- Air/O2 is introduced only after Step 1 is complete.\n- Light and the photocatalyst are essential.\n- The pH 9 buffer suppresses formation of the PMPSCH3 byproduct."

steps.name: Batch Conditions
adjustments: Engineering calculations use the proposal's reactor temperature (35 C), while the batch temperature remains protocol evidence.

steps.name: Kinetics & Residence Time
steps.summary: τ = 30.1 min (council-approved — not re-derived from kinetics). Implied IF = 20× vs batch.
assumptions: τ set by ENGINE council — kinetics estimation bypassed

steps.name: Reactor Sizing
steps.summary: V_R = 5.00 mL, d = 0.75 mm, L = 11.32 m, Pe = 617 (✓ plug flow)

steps.name: Mass Transfer
steps.summary: t_mix = 57.0 s, Da = 0.932 — Kinetically controlled — mixing is not limiting

values.interpretation: Kinetically controlled — mixing is not limiting

assumptions: D = 1e-09 m²/s (typical for small organic molecules in liquid)
Gas holdup estimated from actual reactor gas/liquid volumetric ratio.
O2 solubility uses a water/ethanol-scale Henry-law approximation; validate experimentally for final scale-up.
kLa is a conservative capillary slug-flow estimate tied to gas holdup.

steps.name: Heat Transfer
steps.summary: Q_gen = 0.0239 W, Q_rem = 79.9980 W, Da_th = 0.0003 — Thermally safe

steps.name: Back-Pressure Regulator
steps.summary: BPR REQUIRED: 3.0 bar (Gas-liquid system detected — BPR mandatory to maintain gas solubility (Henry's law: C_gas = H·P) and prevent uncontrolled degassing.)
equations: C_{\mathrm{gas}} = H \cdot P_{\mathrm{partial}}\quad\text{(higher BPR} \Rightarrow \text{more dissolved gas)}

steps.name: Process Metrics
steps.summary: STY = 0.1891 mol/(L·h), P = 0.292 mmol/h, ṅ_lim = 0.0051 mmol/min, startup waste = 4.6 mL, IF = 20×
equations: C_{\mathrm{reactor,inlet}} = C_0 = 0.1000\;\mathrm{M}\quad (\text{single-feed PFR; no dilution at inlet})

_analogies.summary: This photoredox catalysis process involves a radical addition followed by oxidation using fac-[Ir(ppy)3] as the photocatalyst with 425 nm LED irradiation. The reaction was performed in DMSO solvent at 25°C using a MiChS flow photoreactor L-1 (M) with 2 mm ID quartz tubing and a 2.7 mL reactor volume. The flow process achieved a remarkable 30-minute residence time at 0.09 mL/min flow rate, compared to 24 hours required in batch conditions. Flow chemistry provided dramatic improvements with a 48-fold reduction in reaction time (from 24 hours to 30 minutes) and a substantial increase in yield from 22% in batch to 75% in flow. The enhanced performance in flow resulted from improved light penetration and better mass transfer in the thin quartz tubing, enabling more efficient photocatalytic activation and faster reaction kinetics.

### Overall Chemistry Assessment

The assessment of the four candidates reveals significant photonics challenges primarily due to high absorbance exceeding recommended limits, triggering inner-filter effects. The smaller ID choices at 0.75 mm show slightly reduced absorbance but remain high, while the 1.0 mm choices are critically high with A = 1.5. From a chemistry perspective, switching atmospheres between stages is managed well across candidates, maintaining the oxygen-free environment during radical formation and correct reintroduction of oxygen for oxidative steps. Candidates 1 and 3, having longer τ, better align with kinetic requirements, but all require intervention to reduce ID or concentration to mitigate photonic issues. Candidates 2 and 4 exhibit critical high absorbance and mixing limitations, severely impacting selectivity and expected conversion. The photochemical setup evaluated across the candidates reveals a consistent issue with photon penetration, primarily due to high absorbance values stemming from the tubing's ID and the concentration used. Candidate 5 stands slightly ahead in chemistry due to its more favorable kinetic alignment, despite falling into a similar photonics trap as others. All candidates suffer from high Beer-Lambert absorbance, blocking nearly all light from reaching the core of the flow, which critically undermines photonics performance. Correction of this problem is needed for all candidate streams by either reducing concentration or using smaller ID tubing. All candidates are dealing with a major photonics challenge due to extremely high absorbance, leading to complete photon absorption at the reactor wall and zero transmission. This results in a BLOCK for photonics as no light penetrates effectively into the catalyst solution to drive the reaction. Furthermore, there is a redox feasibility issue as the oxidative SET is not feasible with a 0.36 V shortfall, which is a critical chemistry block. Materials are compatible and atmosphere logic is mostly managed, but the SET pathway's fundamental limitation will impede progress. None of the candidates have feasible photon management or electrochemical driving force, so revisions are imperative to address these bottlenecks.

parameters.residence_time_basis: sum of per-stage inlet/STP residence times

stages.atmosphere: Ar (pre-degassed sealed feed, no O2 inlet)
stages.notes: UV-150 standard mode 35°C minimum; BPR on outlet of Stage 2 pressurises entire system including Stage 1.
stages.reactor_name: KHU PFA coil 10 mL, 1.0 mm ID

stages.atmosphere: O2 via KHU-GAS-MFC-O2-BRONKHORST at ~1.12 sccm, T-junction at Stage 1 outlet
stages.notes: FEP coil max 50°C; op at 40°C (fan mode) is within limit. Segmented O2-liquid Taylor flow enhances kLa for aerobic oxidation. BPR placed after Stage 2 outlet.
stages.reactor_name: KHU FEP coil 10 mL, 1.0 mm ID
stages.light_name: KHU manual blue strip LED photoreactor

streams.pump_role: Primary liquid feed pump delivering pre-degassed substrate/photocatalyst solution to Stage 1 reactor
streams.solvent: EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer, 5:1 v/v (pre-degassed offline by Ar sparging or freeze-pump-thaw, loaded into sealed gas-tight reservoir)
streams.reasoning: ṅ_lim=0.0500 mmol/min × eq=1.0 / C_feed=0.1 M = 0.500 mL/min → scaled ×0.152 to 0.0758 mL/min so Σ reactor-feed pumps = Q_reactor_inlet = 0.0758 mL/min

streams.pump_role: Gas feed: O2 delivered by Bronkhorst FLEXI-FLOW Compact O2 MFC into T-junction between Stage 1 outlet and Stage 2 reactor
streams.reasoning: Deterministic gas stoichiometry: inlet/STP MFC flow was recomputed from target gas equivalents (1.00 equiv), liquid flow 0.05118 mL/min, and substrate concentration. Pressure-corrected in-channel gas flow is reported separately; supplied gas equiv = 1.00.

intensification.basis: Predicted screening target: 20.0x residence-time reduction; this is a hypothesis unless the run explicitly selects the intensify policy. Identified batch limitations: mass_transfer_gas_liquid, photon_penetration. Primary flow advantage: mass_transfer. Mechanisms: gas-liquid kLa enhancement (segmented flow), photon penetration via small ID, selectivity-sensitive stream logic. Limitation-driven IF (20x) exceeds class default (6x).
